title: ALMA observations of super-early galaxies: Attenuation-free model predictions
question: Can the FIR dust continuum emission produced by extended, outflow-ejected dust distributions around super-early (z > 10) galaxies predicted by the Attenuation-Free Model be detected by ALMA?

evidence.quote: These estimates are confirmed by detailed calculations performed by Ysard et al. (2019) that we use here.
With these assumptions they indeed find κ large UV ≃ 3 / 4 δ g a = 5085 cm 2 g − 1 , and κ large 88 = 15 cm 2 g − 1 .

recipe.goal: Quantify dust production and total dust mass
recipe.method: Calculate dust-to-stellar mass ratio ξ_d = y_d * ν from SN rate and dust yield per SN, and multiply by stellar mass M_* to obtain dust mass M_d
key_parameters: ν^-1 = 52.9 M_sun per SN, fiducial y_d = 0.1 M_sun/SN, fiducial ξ_d = 1/529, explored range -5 < log ξ_d < -1.6
assumptions: Salpeter IMF in the range 1 - 100 M_sun; dust production dominated by SNe and instantaneous on timescale <= 20 Myr

recipe.goal: Model spatial distribution of dust and optical depth
recipe.method: Compute UV optical depth τ_1500 as a function of dust distribution radius r_d, and determine the radius matching the observed V-band attenuation A_V
key_parameters: κ_1500 = 1.26 x 10^5 cm^2 g^-1 (standard WD01 MW dust); κ_UV^large = 5085 cm^2 g^-1 (large silicate grains, a_0 = 0.5 µm, σ = 0.7, δ_g = 2.95 g cm^-3)
assumptions: Spherical dust distribution of radius r_d; MW-like extinction curve (or geometric absorption cross section for large silicate grains)

recipe.goal: Compute luminosity-weighted and CMB-corrected dust temperature and observed 88 µm continuum flux
recipe.method: Calculate mean dust temperature from UV energy balance (Eq. 1-2), apply radiative transfer slab correction to get luminosity-weighted temperature <T_d>_L and reduced mass M'_d (Eq. 3), apply CMB heating correction T'_d (Eq. 5), and compute observed rest-frame 88 µm flux F_88 against the CMB background (Eq. 4)
assumptions: Flat Universe cosmology (Ω_M = 0.3075, Ω_Λ = 1 - Ω_M, Ω_b = 0.0486, h = 0.6774, σ_8 = 0.826); neglect dust self-heating and scattering
